change: Added Triceps (Triceps Brachii) to secondary. Multiple sources (fitnessvolt, barbend, wellfitinsider) explicitly name triceps as a stabilizing secondary muscle during the rollout — the arms must lock and stabilize throughout the movement. The existing secondary muscles (Lats, Anterior Deltoids, Erector Spinae, Gluteus Maximus) are all confirmed correct and retained.

No changes. Primary glutes + quads and secondary hamstrings + calves are all confirmed by multiple sources. Calves (all 3 heads) are appropriate for stair climbing. Hip flexors (Abductor bucket) were considered but are marginal stabilizers on the stepmill, not a meaningful secondary, so omitted to avoid inflation.

Added glutes (Gluteus Maximus) to secondary. Multiple sources (rb100.fitness, suspensionexercise.co.nz, fitfatherproject) list the glutes as a secondary stabilizer during the suspension fallout — they help maintain the rigid plank position and prevent hip sag throughout the movement. All other entries confirmed correct.

1) Added Lower Traps to mid back primary entry (now Rhomboids, Upper Traps, Lower Traps) — rows involve full trapezius including lower traps for scapular retraction/depression, confirmed by exrx.net and multiple inverted row sources. 2) Added Rotator Cuff (Lats bucket) to secondary — per CLAUDE.md rules, all pulling exercises include Rotator Cuff as secondary. 3) Updated abs secondary to include both Upper Rectus Abdominis and LowerRectus Abdominis (was only Upper Rectus Abdominis) — core bracing in horizontal rows engages the full rectus abdominis isometrically.

1) Added biceps (Biceps Brachii) to secondary — TRX chest fly research (trxtraining.com, fitbod.me, fitfatherproject) consistently lists biceps brachii as a secondary stabilizer (elbow flexion stabilization during fly motion). 2) Updated abs secondary to include both Upper Rectus Abdominis and LowerRectus Abdominis (was only Upper Rectus Abdominis) — full core bracing is engaged isometrically to prevent hip sag. Triceps retained as secondary — confirmed as isometric elbow stabilizer during fly movements. Chest primary (both heads at chest-height handles) confirmed correct.
